sections.h2: How can I sell a house fast in Garland, TX?
sections.html:
A Garland owner can take a cash offer, list with an agent, or sell directly, and the best route depends mostly on whether the house is lived in, rented or carrying a code or tax problem.

Garland has its own Code Compliance Department, which runs a permit program for single-family rentals and short-term rentals. If your house is a rental, that program shapes the sale more than any market trend does. A cash buyer can purchase it as-is and handle the permit transition, while a retail buyer will usually expect an inspected, move-in ready house.

  • Cash offer: no showings, no repair negotiations, closing date set by you.
  • Agent listing: exposure to more buyers, with prep and inspection requests on you.
  • Direct sale: you manage the contract, disclosures and title steps.

sections.h2: What does Garland require of rental houses I want to sell?
sections.html:
Garland requires every single-family rental, duplexes included, to hold a permit from Code Compliance. The city's program page says the permit cannot be assigned or transferred, so a buyer who keeps renting must apply in their own name.

Garland rental permit terms as printed on the city program page
ItemWhat the page says
Single-family rental annual fee$65 on the page, with the renewal fee rising to $250 from Oct. 1, 2026
Short-term rental annual fee$500, with a floor plan and proof of insurance
Single-family inspectionFull inspection at each change of tenancy, unless the property is certified
Short-term inspectionAnnual inspection for renewal
TransferPermit cannot be assigned or transferred

The same page states that the city council was considering an ordinance to treat short-term rentals as a distinct land use, generally allowed by right only in Light Commercial and Heavy Commercial districts and in planned development districts that expressly allow it. A public hearing was set for October 20, 2026. Because that date has passed, call Code Compliance at 972-485-6400 to learn whether the ordinance was adopted and whether it affects your address.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Garland house that has code violations?
sections.html:
Yes. Code violations do not stop a sale, but they can cut buyer interest and need to be disclosed to anyone who asks. A cash buyer is often the easier choice because the house is bought as-is.

If you have received a notice of violation and need more time, the city tells owners to contact their Code Compliance Officer. The department also accepts requests through its online portal and the eAssist app, and its phone line is 972-485-6400. A short extension in writing is useful to hand a buyer along with the notice.

  • Keep a copy of every notice and any extension.
  • Ask the officer what a reinspection would require.
  • Tell the title company about open violations before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: How do delinquent property taxes affect a Garland sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the house, not the person who ignored it. A tax lien attaches on January 1 each year, and a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid.

Texas bills go out around October 1, and taxes unpaid after January 31 become delinquent. On February 1 the collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest. The penalty keeps growing by one percent a month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent, while interest continues at one percent a month. A unit that hires a private attorney can add up to 20 percent more.

Relief exists. Some collectors allow installment plans of up to 36 months on a residence homestead, and a waiver of penalty and interest is possible if you pay by the 21st day after you learn of the delinquency and request it in writing within 181 days of the delinquency date. Ask the tax office that bills your Garland parcel for its payoff total and plan rules.

sections.h2: What if Garland tax delinquency has led to a tax sale?
sections.html:
A tax foreclosure sale is an auction run by a constable or an agent for the taxing unit, and there is no statewide list. Check the county clerk or county tax office sites for upcoming sales.

After such a sale, a former owner of homestead, agricultural or mineral property has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed to redeem, with a premium of 25 percent in the first year or 50 percent in the second, plus the bid, recording fee, taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Other property has a shorter period, 180 days after the deed is filed. Excess sale proceeds can be claimed by the former owner within two years of the sale.

A sale that closes before the auction lets you control the timing and the price. Ask your tax office for a current payoff and a written statement of suits filed.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Garland house?
sections.html:
You can sell an inherited house, but title must be in order first, and a homestead exemption may need new paperwork. Heirs not named on a recorded deed must give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim the exemption.

A transfer on death deed passes real property without probate if it was recorded in the county before the owner died. A Lady Bird deed lets the owner sell or mortgage without the beneficiary's consent. If neither exists, ask the county clerk about probate filings, since the clerk also handles applications and small estate affidavits.

Many heirs in this situation do not want to repair and list a house they do not live in, so a documented as-is cash sale is a common choice.

sections.h2: What should I ask a cash buyer about a Garland rental?
sections.html:
Ask who will apply for the new permit, who pays for any inspection, and how existing tenants will be treated. Those three answers decide whether the closing runs smoothly.

  • Whether the offer is as-is, including any items the city inspection might flag.
  • Whether the buyer takes over the lease and the security deposit, or needs the house vacant.
  • Who covers the permit fee and the inspection at the change of tenancy.
  • What the closing date is and which title company will handle the funds.

Put every answer in the written contract. If the house is a short-term rental, also confirm that the buyer understands the annual inspection and insurance steps the city lists for renewal.

sections.h2: What happens to recording and closing in Garland?
sections.html:
Your deed is recorded with the county clerk of the county where the property sits, and must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other officer authorized to take acknowledgments.

The Texas Courts clerk manual lists a $5.00 fee for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus records management, archive and technology fees that vary by county. Ask the title company for the exact total and the payoff of every lien. If foreclosure notices are pending, notice of sale must be filed with the clerk and posted at least 21 days ahead, which gives you a clear deadline for closing.

faqs.q: Can a Garland rental permit transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The city's program page says the permit cannot be assigned or transferred, so the buyer applies in their own name if they will rent the house.

faqs.q: Did Garland adopt the new short-term rental rules?
faqs.a: A hearing was set for October 20, 2026. Call Garland Code Compliance at 972-485-6400 to learn the outcome and whether it affects your address.

faqs.q: What does it cost to keep a Garland single-family rental permitted?
faqs.a: The city page printed $65 a year, with renewals rising to $250 beginning October 1, 2026. Short-term rental permits were printed at $500 a year.

faqs.q: When do Garland property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Taxes unpaid after January 31 are delinquent, and a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added on February 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Garland house before a tax foreclosure auction?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale that pays the taxes at closing clears the lien, and doing it before the auction avoids redemption rules and court costs.
